findings.problem: EventWorkflow uses bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) and a String status to model lifecycle state, making illegal states constructable — e.g. is_sent=true with status="draft", or is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(123).
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can set inconsistent fields producing logically impossible workflow states that bypass type-system enforcement.
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool with a single EventStatus enum typestate. Remove sent_at_epoch_ms or tie it inside the variant so it only exists when the event is in the sent state.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive string for a domain lifecycle concept. Any string value is valid, including garbage like "banana" or "SENT".
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code branch on string equality; invalid values silently propagate instead of being rejected at construction.
findings.fix: Define a sealed EventStatus enum { Draft, Validating, Validated, Sent } and replace String with EventStatus.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate lifecycle flags. Boolean lifecycle flags are explicitly called out in the reference as requiring replacement with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: Two independent booleans create 4 combinations but the domain has fewer valid states. Invalid cross-combinations (e.g. validated but not sent when that should be required) are representable.
findings.fix: Merge into a single EventStatus enum typestate that encodes all valid lifecycle transitions.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool and sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> redundantly encode sent-ness. The timestamp exists independently of the boolean, so an event can be not-sent yet have a timestamp, or sent with no timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: State inconsistency: callers must coordinate two fields. A bug in one field leaves the other stale, producing divergent state views.
findings.fix: Fold the timestamp into the typestate: EventStatus::Sent { sent_at: u64 }. The field only exists in the sent variant, making the redundant boolean unnecessary.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes EventWorkflow and returns EventWorkflow — no typestate transition. It mutates fields in place (item.status = "sent"; item.is_sent = true) instead of returning a distinct type.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can call mark_sent multiple times, or skip it entirely, with no compile-time enforcement of a single transition. The function does not prevent calling it on an already-sent event.
findings.fix: Change to fn mark_sent(from: EventStatus) -> Result<EventStatus, MarkSentError> returning a new typestate variant, or make EventWorkflow private with a constructor that enforces the transition.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() uses a magic string literal for a domain state transition.
findings.failure_mode: Typos, casing mismatches, and extra whitespace silently produce invalid states. Refactoring the status vocabulary requires searching string literals instead of a single enum.
findings.fix: Use the enum variant directly: EventStatus::Sent { sent_at }. No string literals needed.

findings.problem: All fields of EventWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to construct and mutate the struct directly without any domain invariants.
findings.failure_mode: External code can create EventWorkflow with any field combination, entirely bypassing the intended lifecycle.
findings.fix: Make fields private. Provide a private constructor or builder that enforces invariants. Better yet, replace the struct entirely with the typestate enum.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs mutation (setting fields) rather than returning a pure, immutable new state. The function signature accepts and returns the same mutable struct type.
findings.failure_mode: Side effects are embedded in the core instead of being isolated to the shell. Pure calculations should produce new values, not mutate existing ones.
findings.fix: Return a new value: fn mark_sent(event: &EventWorkflow) -> Result<NewEvent, Error> producing an immutable result, or use the typestate enum pattern where the returned type encodes the new state.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has fundamental architectural violations — primitive obsession, boolean lifecycle flags, redundant state fields, and absent typestate patterns — that make illegal states fully representable. These require structural refactoring, not local fixes.
